portInfo.description: ROSTOCK PORT GmbH’s cruise product is the Warnemünde Cruise Center, opened 1 May 2005 — a ~3,000 m² terminal building with customs/Federal Police clearance rooms and claimed capacity for passenger change-overs of up to 2,500 people per day. Passenger information stresses the unique rail adjacency among German passenger harbours and that the seaside resort of Warnemünde starts immediately behind the quay. Rostock city centre is cited at about 20 minutes; Berlin about 2 hours by train or bus. SeaDays catalog mapping notes a live redirect from this slug toward a Warnemünde–Berlin marketing page — research keeps rostock-germany as its own obligation and does not invent a shared port_id.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Warnemünde Cruise Center (berths P7 / P8) — Am Passagierkai 3, 18119 Rostock-Warnemünde
gettingThere.distanceToCity: On foot into Warnemünde: resort begins behind the quay. Rail: ~500 m / 5 minutes from Warnemünde station; peak S-Bahn-style intervals cited as every 7.5 minutes to Rostock Hbf in season (confirm live VVW schedules). Berlin: ~2 h train/bus — only with a long call and strict return buffer. Parking at the cruise terminal during calls is restricted.

topThings: Warnemünde lighthouse / Alter Strom / beach — ~90 min.
Rostock city centre (Neustadt / university quarter) — ~20 min transfer cited; hours not verified.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Do not park at the cruise terminal during a call — use published alternatives.
